Description: September 3, 2026; flagship for the hardest end-to-end coding, computer use, and research work; a single dense reasoning model with five effort settings, a 1.05M-token context window, and 128K max output; saturates FrontierMath Tier 4 at 97.6% and ARC-AGI-3 at 99.9%, and hits 100% on ExploitBench; $10/$50 per million input/output tokens, 2.5x the GPT-5.6 Sol rate, with prompts over 272,000 tokens billed at double input; rollout began with enterprise customers in OpenAI's Daybreak cybersecurity program

September 2, 2026; fourth Flash release in under four months, tuned for long-horizon coding and autonomous agents; 89.4% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 73.7% on DeepSWE v1.1, and 59.0% on OSWorld 2.0, beating Claude Opus 5 on three of Google's published benchmarks; 1M-token context, 64K output, with text, image, audio, video, and PDF input; $0.75/$3.75 per million tokens, unchanged from 3.7 Flash, with both figures set to double on January 1, 2027

September 2, 2026; frontier proprietary reasoning model with significant coding and agentic gains, built to sustain long-horizon work across multiple workflows in a single thread; 1M-token context with text, image, and video input; ranks #6 of 636 models on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index; $1.25/$4.25 per million tokens through Muse Code and the Meta Model API, with a contributor endpoint 10 to 20 times cheaper for developers who let Meta train on their data

September 1, 2026; 55.8% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, 73.4% on CursorBench 3.2.0, and 52.6% on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, more than double Fable 5; 1M-token context and 128K max output; cache reads cut 75% to $0.25 per million, lowering typical workload costs about 25% and highly agentic workloads up to 45%; $10/$50 per million input/output tokens; now cleared to identify software vulnerabilities, with roughly 60% fewer cyber safeguard interventions per Claude Code session

September 1, 2026; the same model as Fable 5.1 with more permissive safeguards for vetted cyberdefenders and life scientists; 60.9% on Terminal-Bench 4.0; available through the Cyber Verification Program and the Life Sciences Verification Program, and now powers Claude Security

August 26, 2026; the stealth "OX Alpha" model that topped coding leaderboards anonymously, revealed and open-sourced; 320B total / 18B active natively multimodal hybrid-attention MoE, the first multimodal model in the GLM-5 family, with a 1,048,576-token context window and image and video input; beats GLM-5.2 across benchmarks at roughly one-tenth the price, landing within half a point of Claude Opus 4.8 on Z.ai's internal coding benchmark; $0.075/$0.25 per million tokens; MIT license, weights on Hugging Face

API-only flagship released August 14, 2026, with weights following August 28; focused on software engineering, autonomous agents, and cybersecurity; same MoE architecture as GLM-5.2 at roughly 750B total parameters, with Z.ai attributing the gains to post-training on real-world expert workflows rather than a larger model; 1M-token context and 128K output; 50% coding improvement over GLM-5.2 on its internal Code Bench, 66.9 on DeepSWE v1.1 (up from 46.2), and 84.5% on CyberGym, narrowly ahead of Claude Mythos 5; API access through the GLM Coding Plan starting at $18/month; breaking with GLM-5.2's MIT license, ships under a bespoke "glm-5.3" license requiring any Model-as-a-Service business clearing $10B in trailing 12-month revenue to pass a Z.ai security review

August 14, 2026; dense 27B open-weights model accepting text, image, and video, the smaller companion to Qwen3.8-Max; native 262,144-token context extensible to 1M; outperforms Claude Opus 4.6 Max on 16 of the 24 benchmarks in its official model card, with the largest wins in agentic coding (61.7 vs 53.4 on SWE-bench Pro), instruction following (79.5 vs 62.5 on IFBench), and computer use (84.3 vs 72.7 on OSWorld-Verified); 90.3% on LiveCodeBench v6; Apache 2.0 license

August 13, 2026; V4 Pro leaves preview for general availability across the app, web, and API; adds three reasoning-effort levels and native OpenAI Responses API compatibility, with endpoint identifiers unchanged; 1M-token context with output up to 384,000 tokens; tiered pricing took effect August 16, with off-peak usage at half the peak rate

August 12, 2026; built for long-running agents, agentic coding, and interactive visual work, with a 500K-token context window and a new xhigh effort tier; big jumps over Grok 4.5 on DeepSWE (54 to 65.9) and APEX-Agents (47.1 to 57.5), scoring 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index to match GPT-5.6 Sol; LiveBench agentic coding regressed, 56.5 to 54.2, the one measured step backward; $2/$6 per million tokens with cached input at $0.50, rising to $4/$12 for prompts of 200K or more

August 5, 2026; a coding-focused release shipped alongside Muse Code, Meta's terminal coding agent, co-trained with the model it runs on; 82.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 59.3% on DeepSWE 1.1, second only to Claude Opus 5 on Meta's own comparison table, though 1.2 was benchmarked inside Muse Code while 1.1 was benchmarked on mini-swe-agent, so the gain reflects model plus harness; Meta said on August 10 that open weights are coming, without a date

August 3, 2026, following the July 19 WAIC preview; 2.4T-parameter multimodal flagship for autonomous long-horizon coding and knowledge work, with vision as a continuous feedback loop for planning, execution, and self-correction rather than static input; Alibaba highlights 10+ day runs from an empty repository to production, 500+ turns of chip-design optimization, and 365 days of simulated e-commerce strategy; $2.00/$6.00 per million tokens with implicit caching at $0.25; open weights followed August 12 as Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, the first downloadable Max-class Qwen, 2.4T total with 95B active, though the checkpoint is text-only with thinking forced on and ships under a custom license rather than the Apache 2.0 used for the 27B sibling

July 24, 2026; new default on Claude Max and strongest model on Claude Pro, approaching Fable 5's frontier intelligence at half the price; new state of the art on Frontier-Bench and GDPval-AA, more than doubling Opus 4.8's Frontier-Bench score; on CursorBench 3.2 at max effort, comes within 0.5% of Fable 5's peak at half the cost; three times the next-best model on ARC-AGI 3; remains behind Mythos 5 on biology research and exploit development, though close on vulnerability identification; Anthropic's automated behavioral audit found it the most aligned model to date; $5/$25 per million tokens, with Fast mode at 2.5x speed for double the price

July 16, 2026; the world's first open 3T-class model, 2.8T total parameters on a new Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals architecture, with native vision and a 1M-token context window; Stable LatentMoE activates 16 of 896 experts for roughly 2.5x better scaling efficiency than Kimi K2; Moonshot says it trails Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol overall but leads on several benchmarks, including 88.3% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 81.2% on FrontierSWE, and 91.2% on BrowseComp; $0.30/$3.00/$15.00 per million tokens for cache-hit input, cache-miss input, and output; weights released July 26 on Hugging Face at ~594GB in native MXFP4, under a custom "kimi-k3" license requiring Model-as-a-Service businesses over $20M in trailing 12-month revenue to sign a separate commercial agreement; Moonshot calls it "open weight," not "open source"

July 15, 2026; the lab's first release, an open-weights MoE transformer with 975B total / 41B active parameters, up to 1M-token context, pretrained on 45 trillion tokens across text, images, audio, and video; supports controllable thinking effort and native multimodal reasoning rather than optimizing for a single benchmark; 77.6% on SWE-Bench Verified, 54.3% on SWE-Bench Pro Public, and 63.8% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, reaching Nemotron 3 Ultra's Terminal-Bench score at roughly one-third the tokens; shipped with a preview of Inkling-Small, a 276B/12B-active sibling that matches or exceeds it on several benchmarks; full weights including an NVFP4 checkpoint on Hugging Face, fine-tunable on the lab's Tinker platform, with API access via Together, Fireworks, Modal, Databricks, and Baseten

July 9, 2026; three-tier family where the number marks the generation and each name marks a durable capability tier that can advance on its own schedule; Sol is the flagship for complex coding, cybersecurity, and long-running agentic work at $5/$30 per million tokens; Terra is the balanced everyday tier, competitive with GPT-5.5 at about half the cost, at $2.50/$15; Luna is the fastest and cheapest at $1/$6; Sol with max reasoning sets a new state of the art on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index at 80, plus new highs on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and DeepSWE; introduces max reasoning effort and an ultra mode that runs subagents concurrently; all three tiers are classified at OpenAI's "High" risk level for cyber and biological/chemical capability

July 9, 2026; multimodal reasoning model for agentic tool use, computer use, and coding, with a 1M-token context window and support for orchestrating multi-agent systems as either primary agent or subagent; handles large codebases including bug diagnosis, feature implementation, and large-scale migrations; 61.5% on SWE-Bench Pro, 80.0% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, and 53.3% on DeepSWE 1.1; leads its benchmark comparison on several agentic evals, including 88.1% on MCP Atlas, 54.7% on JobBench, and 62.1% on Humanity's Last Exam with tools, ahead of Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 4.8, and GPT-5.5; launched with the public preview of the Meta Model API, Meta's first paid developer offering, at $1.25/$4.25 per million tokens; early partners include Replit, Cline, and Box

July 8, 2026; MoE model trained jointly by the two companies, Cursor's first built for more than software engineering, spanning data science, finance, legal work, and other knowledge domains; trained on trillions of tokens of Cursor usage data plus reinforcement learning on difficult problems built by a distributed agent system; new cybersecurity safeguards detect and block bad actors outright rather than silently downgrading intelligence; available in Cursor across desktop, web, iOS, CLI, and SDK; $2/$6 per million tokens for the base model, $4/$18 for the fast variant; a distinct model class from Composer 2.5, which Cursor continues to offer separately

July 8, 2026; proprietary software-engineering model trained on a Kimi K2.7 base with a refined reinforcement-learning recipe, optimized for long-horizon asynchronous coding; 42.3% on Cognition's own FrontierCode benchmark and about 81.5% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, which the company positions as within a few points of Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5; runs at 1,000 tokens per second via Cerebras at $1.97 per task; available inside Devin on Web, Desktop, and CLI; not open source, and the benchmark and cost claims come from Cognition's own launch materials rather than independent testing

July 6, 2026, following the April 23 preview; 295B total / 21B active MoE with an additional 3.8B-parameter MTP layer, built on a hybrid fast-and-slow-thinking architecture; 57.9% on SWE-bench Pro, 68.3% on SWE-bench Multilingual, 45.6% on NL2repo, and 71.7% on Terminal Bench 2.1, which Tencent says is competitive with GLM-5.1 and GLM-5.2; positioned as a cost-efficient model for software development, office work, financial modeling, front-end design, and game production, with two to five times better parameter efficiency than flagship models; 256K context; Apache 2.0, available day one on Hugging Face and ModelScope, with progressive rollout to OpenRouter, Cline, and Kilo; API live on Tencent Cloud TokenHub

redeployed July 1, 2026 after a brief export-control suspension; a Mythos-class model made safe for general use via safety classifiers that fall back to Opus 4.8 on cybersecurity, biology/chemistry, and distillation queries; state of the art on software engineering, vision, knowledge work, and long-horizon agentic tasks; scored highest among frontier models on Cognition's FrontierCode evaluation; $10/$50 per million tokens

redeployed July 1, 2026 after a brief export-control suspension; the same underlying model as Fable 5 with all safeguards lifted; not generally available, restricted to vetted Project Glasswing cyberdefense and critical infrastructure partners, with a separate trusted access program for biomedical researchers planned; $10/$50 per million tokens

June 30, 2026; most agentic Sonnet yet, with performance close to Opus 4.8 at a lower price; default model for Free and Pro plans, also available in Claude Code and the Claude Platform; cyber safeguards enabled by default but substantially weaker cyber capabilities than Opus 4.8 and Mythos 5; introductory pricing $2/$10 per million tokens through August 31, 2026, then $3/$15

June 30, 2026; 1.6T-parameter MoE coding and agentic model with ~48B activated parameters per token, a 1M-token context window via LongCat Sparse Attention, and 35T+ pretraining tokens; trained entirely on a 50,000-card domestic AI ASIC cluster with no Nvidia hardware, a first at this scale for non-Nvidia training; previously ran anonymously on OpenRouter as "Owl Alpha," where it led developer usage charts for two months; 59.5 SWE-Bench Pro, 70.8 Terminal-Bench 2.1, 77.3 SWE-Bench Multilingual; MIT licensed; API priced at $0.75/$2.95 per million tokens with no charge for cache hits

June 23, 2026; not a coding model but a world model for simulating coding and agent environments; predicts the next environment state given an agent's action and history across seven domains including Terminal, SWE, Web, and OS; built on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base, 35B total / 3B active, 262K context, Apache 2.0; a larger 397B-A17B variant tops its own AgentWorldBench; useful for training and evaluating coding agents rather than writing code directly

June 22, 2026; not a standalone model but a multi-agent orchestration system delivered as one OpenAI-compatible API, shipping in two tiers (Fugu and Fugu Ultra); dynamically assembles and coordinates a pool of existing frontier models per task, drawing on two ICLR 2026 papers (TRINITY and Conductor) on learned model orchestration; reports SWE-Bench Pro 73.7 and TerminalBench 2.1 82.1 for Fugu Ultra, though benchmarks compare the orchestrated ensemble against single frontier models and the underlying model pool is proprietary and undisclosed; positioned explicitly as frontier capability without export-control exposure; Fugu Ultra priced at $5/$30 per million tokens; not available in the EU/EEA

launched June 13, 2026 with MIT open weights released June 16; flagship long-horizon and coding model in the GLM-5 family; 744B-parameter MoE with ~40B active per token and a solid 1M-token context window; introduces IndexShare, which reuses one indexer across every four sparse attention layers to cut per-token FLOPs by 2.9x at 1M context, plus an improved MTP layer that lifts speculative-decoding acceptance length by up to 20%; multiple thinking-effort levels (High and Max); 62.1 SWE-bench Pro, 81.0 Terminal-Bench 2.1, 63.7 ProgramBench; no regional limits

June 12, 2026; coding-focused agentic model built on Kimi K2.6; 1T total / 32B active MoE with 256K context, native INT4 quantization, and multimodal input (image and video) via a 400M-parameter MoonViT vision encoder; improves long-horizon coding task completion while cutting thinking-token usage roughly 30% versus K2.6; open weights under Modified MIT License

June 9, 2026; 30B total / 3B active open-weight MoE model optimized for code generation, agentic software engineering, and terminal tasks; 256K context window with 64K max output; decoder-only sparse MoE using interleaved sliding-window and global attention; post-trained with cascaded SFT followed by reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR); released under Apache 2.0

June 4, 2026; 550B total parameters, 55B active; open-weight hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE built for long-running agentic coding and orchestration workflows; scores 48 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, making it the highest-scoring open-weight model from a US lab at release; 65–70.4% on SWE-bench Verified; up to 5x higher inference throughput than comparable open models; weights, training recipes, and quantized variants all released publicly

June 1, 2026; first open-weight model to combine frontier-level coding, a 1M-token context window, and native multimodal input (text, image, video) in a single architecture; uses new MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) design; 59.0% SWE-Bench Pro; API live at launch, open weights committed to Hugging Face and GitHub within ten days
